bundle.name: Northern Spain: Donostia, Bilbao, the Picos and Santiago
bundle.description: Nine days along the green coast — pintxo bars, one grill, one museum, one gorge, and a cathedral at the end.

trips.name: Northern Spain: San Sebastián → Bilbao → Picos → Santiago
trips.summary: Nine days of eating and walking, driving west along the Cantabrian coast.

days.label: Land in Bilbao, drive straight to Donostia

stops.title: Flight into Bilbao (BIO)
stops.notes: Outbound leg only; the flight home from Santiago is priced on day nine. Flying into one end and out of the other is what makes this route work without a day of backtracking — the open-jaw fare is barely more than a return.

stops.title: Collect the hire car at the airport
stops.notes: Take it from the airport, not from central Bilbao: the city desks shut at 13:00 on Saturdays, and the Picos leg is impossible without a car. Booked a one-way drop at Santiago airport, which costs about €90 extra and saves two days.

stops.title: Drive the AP-8 to San Sebastián
stops.notes: Take the toll road and pay the €12. The free N-634 through the hills is an hour longer and full of trucks. Park in the underground at Okendo rather than hunting a street space in the Parte Vieja, which is resident-permit only.

stops.title: Check in at Lasala Plaza Hotel

location.name: Lasala Plaza Hotel, Plaza de Lasala

stops.notes: Three nights on the harbour edge of the old town. Everything on the next two evenings is within four hundred metres, which matters more than the room: a pintxo crawl that ends in a taxi is not a pintxo crawl.

stops.title: Opening night: Bar Zeruko and Ganbara

location.name: Bar Zeruko and Bar Ganbara, Calle Fermín Calbetón

stops.notes: Two bars, no more, on a night that started at an airport. Zeruko for the theatrical ones and Ganbara for the sautéed wild mushrooms with an egg yolk — the mushrooms are ordered from the barman, not taken off the counter, and this is the single most common mistake visitors make.

days.label: Donostia: the bay, Monte Igueldo, and a proper crawl

stops.title: Breakfast at Pastelería Otaegui
stops.notes: The old pastry shop on the edge of the Parte Vieja. Ask for a pantxineta, which is the local almond and cream thing and is what everyone is queuing for at eleven.

stops.title: La Concha end to end, and the Peine del Viento

location.name: Playa de la Concha and Peine del Viento

stops.notes: Go at high tide. Chillida's sculptures are the photograph, but the blowholes cut into the paving in front of them only fire when there is swell — at low water it is three lumps of iron and a puddle.

stops.title: Funicular up Monte Igueldo
stops.notes: 1912 wooden funicular, four euros return, and the view down the whole shell of the bay that every postcard uses. The rickety amusement park at the top is genuinely 1920s and genuinely rickety.

stops.title: The tortilla at Bar Néstor
stops.notes: Néstor makes one tortilla at 13:00 and one at 20:00, twelve slices each, and that is the entire supply. You put your name on the list at noon or you do not eat it. Order the tomato salad and a txuleta while you wait — that is the actual meal; the tortilla is a slice.

stops.title: Up Monte Urgull to the Mota castle

location.name: Castillo de la Mota, Monte Urgull

stops.notes: Twenty-five minutes up from behind the aquarium, free, and almost nobody does it. The 1813 siege museum inside the castle explains why the old town is entirely 19th-century — the answer is that the British and Portuguese burned it down.

stops.title: Txakoli and anchovies at Bar Txepetxa
stops.notes: One thing, done nine ways: anchovies, cured in-house, on bread, with a different topping each time. Have the one with sea urchin and the plain one, and let them pour the txakoli from height.

stops.title: The crawl: Cuchara de San Telmo, Gandarias, Borda Berri

location.name: Calle 31 de Agosto and Calle Fermín Calbetón

stops.notes: One or two pintxos and one small glass per bar, then move — sitting down anywhere ends the crawl. Order the carrillera at Cuchara and the risotto de idiazábal at Borda Berri; both are cooked to order, so nothing on the counter is what you want.

days.label: Getaria: the grill, the museum, and the vines

stops.title: Breakfast at the hotel

location.name: Lasala Plaza Hotel, Plaza de Lasala

stops.title: Coast road to Getaria via Zarautz

location.name: N-634 coast road, Zarautz to Getaria

stops.notes: Take the coast road today, not the motorway — it runs along the cliff above the txakoli terraces and the last bend into Getaria is the view of the Mouse island. Park in the harbour car park; the village is one street and it is pedestrian.

stops.title: Cristóbal Balenciaga Museoa
stops.notes: He was born in this village and the collection is the actual garments, not photographs of them. Closed Mondays outside July and August, which catches people out. Booked the 11:00 slot to leave a clean hour before lunch.

stops.title: Lunch at Elkano
stops.notes: The whole turbot off the charcoal is the reason to come and it is sold by weight for two — you will be quoted at the table, and it is not cheap. Booked six weeks out. Eat the cheeks and the gelatinous bits round the head; the waiter will show you how and it is the best part.

stops.title: Txakoli tasting at Txomin Etxaniz
stops.notes: Provisional — visits must be booked and one of you has to not drink, because it is a switchback road back down to the N-634. The vines are trained high on wires so the sea wind dries them; that is the whole explanation of why the wine tastes like it does.

stops.title: Quiet dinner at Bodegón Alejandro
stops.notes: Floated as the antidote to two nights of standing up. A basement dining room and a fixed menu of classics; whether anyone wants dinner after turbot at two is a decision for about six o'clock.

days.label: West to Bilbao and the Guggenheim

stops.title: Breakfast, and check out of the Lasala

location.name: Lasala Plaza Hotel, Plaza de Lasala

stops.title: Drive San Sebastián to Bilbao
stops.notes: Eighty minutes on the toll road. Bilbao's centre is a low-emission zone — leave the car in the hotel garage on arrival and do not move it again until Saturday morning.

stops.title: Check in at Hotel Miró
stops.notes: Two nights, directly opposite the Guggenheim and a fifteen-minute walk from the Casco Viejo — which is the right side of the river to be on for this trip.

stops.title: Pintxos in Plaza Nueva: Gure Toki and Víctor Montes
stops.notes: Bilbao's pintxos are bigger, cheaper and less clever than Donostia's and that is not a criticism. Gure Toki does the inventive ones; Víctor Montes is the belle-époque room with the counter you photograph. Sunday morning the square is a stamp and antiques market and the bars are heaving by eleven.

stops.title: Guggenheim Bilbao
stops.notes: Timed slot booked; closed Mondays except in August. Do the Richard Serra room first — it is on the ground floor and people walk past it looking for the stairs, then run out of attention before they come back. The audio guide is included and unusually good on the building itself.

stops.title: Walk the Nervión: Zubizuri, the Deusto bank, back past Maman

location.name: Nervión riverside walk and Zubizuri bridge

stops.notes: Cross at the Zubizuri and come back down the far bank — the titanium reads completely differently from Deusto in evening light, and it is the only angle where the building looks like a ship rather than a flower.

stops.title: Dinner at Mina
stops.notes: Held, not confirmed — one Michelin star, twenty covers, and a tasting menu only. Across the river from the Casco Viejo on the old dockside; walk it, ten minutes, rather than getting a taxi to circle the one-way system.

days.label: The light day: Bilbao on no plan

stops.title: Mercado de la Ribera, before noon

location.name: Mercado de la Ribera, Erribera Kalea

stops.notes: One of the largest covered markets in Europe and a working one — go before noon on a weekday, because by one the bar tables belong to people who work nearby and by two the fishmongers are packing up. Coffee and a pintxo at the counter inside is three or four euros.

stops.title: The Siete Calles, with nothing to see

location.name: Siete Calles and Catedral de Santiago

stops.notes: Deliberately unstructured. The seven streets are the original medieval town; the Catedral de Santiago on Calle Santiago is a stop on the coastal Camino and takes fifteen minutes. Everything else here is shops and that is fine.

stops.title: Txikiteo in Plaza Nueva, then dinner at Los Fueros

location.name: Bar Restaurante Los Fueros, Calle Los Fueros

stops.notes: Txikiteo is the Bilbao word for the crawl — small glasses, one bar at a time, standing. Los Fueros dates from 1878 and is the oldest bar in the city; it is small, it is booked, and it does the classics properly rather than cleverly.

days.label: Into Asturias: Cangas de Onís and the Covadonga lakes

stops.title: Breakfast, check out of the Miró
Drive the A-8 to Cangas de Onís
stops.notes: Three hours with one stop, and free the whole way. The viaducts near Unquera where the road crosses the Deva are the best part of the drive; the services at Torrelavega are the only decent ones.

stops.title: Check in at the Parador de Cangas de Onís

location.name: Parador de Cangas de Onís, Villanueva

stops.notes: Two nights in a 12th-century monastery on the Sella, three kilometres out of the town. Being outside Cangas is the point — the town is a car park in August and the river bank here is silent.

stops.title: Cider and lunch at El Molín de la Pedrera

location.name: El Molín de la Pedrera, Calle Río Güeña

stops.notes: Let the waiter pour the sidra from above his head — it is not showing off. Natural cider is flat and the fall aerates it, which is why you get a finger of it at a time and drink each pour straight down. Order the cachopo to share between two, never one each.

stops.title: Covadonga and the lakes, by shuttle bus
stops.notes: From Easter to October the mountain road is closed to private cars — you park at El Repelao or in Cangas and take the shuttle, and the combined ticket covers the basilica stop too. Go late: the last bus down is around 20:00 and the crowds thin after five, when the light on Enol is worth the whole day.

stops.title: Dinner at the Parador

location.name: Parador de Cangas de Onís, Villanueva

stops.notes: Eating in tonight because tomorrow starts at half past seven. Ask them at dinner for the packed lunch for the Cares — they do it for hikers and it needs a day's notice.

days.label: The Ruta del Cares, all of it

stops.title: Early breakfast, and collect the packed lunch

location.name: Parador de Cangas de Onís, Villanueva

stops.notes: Two litres of water each, minimum. There is no water and no shade for eleven kilometres and the gorge holds heat like an oven.

stops.title: Drive to Poncebos and park
stops.notes: Poncebos fills by nine in summer and the overflow is a kilometre back down the road, which adds twenty minutes at each end of an already long day. The road in from Arenas is single-track with passing places and a bus comes the other way.

stops.title: Poncebos to Caín and back through the gorge
stops.notes: 22 km out and back, six hours moving, and the whole climb is in the first three kilometres on the way out — which means the hard part happens while it is still cool and the return is downhill and shaded. The path is a maintenance ledge cut for a hydro canal: no railing, a long drop, and not a walk for anyone who does not like exposure. No phone signal inside the gorge.

stops.title: Cabrales cheese in Arenas

location.name: Cueva Exposición del Queso de Cabrales, Arenas de Cabrales

stops.notes: Nobody has committed to this and after six hours of walking it may not survive. Twenty minutes inside an actual maturing cave, and they sell the cheese cheaper than the shops in Cangas do.

stops.title: Dinner at El Polesu

location.name: Sidrería El Polesu, Avenida de Covadonga

stops.notes: A cider house rather than a restaurant: bottles by the bottle, cheese boards, and fabada if anyone can face it. Loud, tiled, and exactly right after a long day on a ledge.

days.label: West along the coast to Santiago

stops.title: Breakfast, and check out of the Parador

location.name: Parador de Cangas de Onís, Villanueva

stops.title: A-8 west, and the walk down to Playa del Silencio
stops.notes: Park at the top and walk down the steps — it is a pebble cove inside a rock amphitheatre and there is nothing at the bottom, no bar, no toilet, no shade. Fifteen minutes down and twenty back up, and the only reason to stop between Asturias and Galicia.

stops.title: Lunch on the harbour at Cudillero
stops.notes: The village is a stack of painted houses round a slipway and it is a hard place to eat badly. Park in the upper car park and walk down; the harbour itself is a turning circle and you will regret driving into it.

stops.title: Cudillero to Santiago de Compostela

location.name: A-8 and AG-64, Asturias into Galicia

stops.notes: Four hours. The A-8 turns inland after Ribadeo and the last stretch on the AG-64 is slower than the map suggests — leave Cudillero by two if you want to be checked in before dinner. Fuel is cheaper in Asturias than in Galicia; fill before Ribadeo.

stops.title: Check in at the Hostal dos Reis Católicos

location.name: Parador Hostal dos Reis Católicos, Praza do Obradoiro

stops.notes: Two nights in the 1499 pilgrims' hospital on the cathedral square — arguably the oldest hotel in the world and the reason the last two days are worth planning around. Parking is a garage five minutes away, not the square; they give you a permit to unload.

stops.title: First look at the Obradoiro at dusk
stops.notes: Unplanned and better for it. The square empties after eight when the day's pilgrims have gone to eat, the floodlights come on, and someone is usually playing a gaita under the arch into Praza da Quintana.

stops.title: Dinner at O Curro da Parra

location.name: O Curro da Parra, Rúa do Curro da Parra

stops.notes: Held for two upstairs — the ground floor is the tapas bar and takes no bookings, the dining room above does. Galician cooking with a lighter hand than most of the old town; the weekday lunch menu is a third of the price if the plan changes.

days.label: Santiago: the roof, the market, the mass, and home

stops.title: Coffee and tarta de Santiago at Café Literarios
stops.notes: Tables on the Quintana with the cathedral's Puerta Santa in front of you, and it opens before the tour groups arrive.

stops.title: Cathedral rooftop tour: the Cubiertas
stops.notes: Booked online days ahead — it is the only way onto the granite roof and the slots genuinely sell out. Guided, an hour, and it goes ahead in rain, which in Santiago is the normal condition. Flat shoes, no exceptions at the door.

stops.title: Mercado de Abastos

location.name: Mercado de Abastos, Rúa das Ameas

stops.notes: Buy at a stall — percebes, scallops, a wedge of tetilla — and carry it to one of the kitchens in the market that will cook what you bought for a few euros a plate. That is the trick here and almost no visitor uses it.

stops.title: Pilgrims' Mass at noon
stops.notes: Free, open to everyone, and full by 11:30. The Botafumeiro only swings when a group has paid for it — the cathedral publishes which masses have one the day before, so check that page rather than hoping. Bags go through a scanner at the door and large rucksacks are refused.

stops.title: Lunch at Abastos 2.0
stops.notes: No menu; they cook what came into the market that morning and tell you what it is. Held two seats at the counter — it is a converted market stall with about a dozen places and it does not do a second sitting.

stops.title: Drop the hire car at Santiago airport

location.name: Santiago–Rosalía de Castro Airport (SCQ), car hire returns

stops.notes: Fill up at the Repsol on the N-634 by the airport turn — the return desk charges a refuelling fee that is roughly double the pump. Twelve kilometres from the old town, twenty minutes.

stops.title: Flight home from Santiago (SCQ)
stops.notes: Return half of the open-jaw fare booked on day one. SCQ is small and the security queue is short, but there is almost nothing airside — do the eating in the market, not here.

backlog.title: Asador Etxebarri in Axpe

location.name: Asador Etxebarri, Plaza San Juan, Atxondo

backlog.notes: Everything cooked over wood, including the ice cream. An hour inland from Bilbao and it books out a year ahead — on the list because the list is where it will stay unless a cancellation appears.

backlog.title: San Juan de Gaztelugatxe and the Bermeo coast
backlog.notes: 241 steps out to a hermitage on a rock. Free but timed-entry ticketed and the slots go weeks in advance; it would cost the light day in Bilbao, which is a bad trade.

backlog.title: Fuente Dé cable car and the Cantabrian side of the Picos
backlog.notes: 750 m of ascent in four minutes and a high plateau at the top. It is on the far side of the massif from Cangas — two hours' drive each way, so it only works if the Cares gets rained off.

backlog.title: Finisterre and the Costa da Morte
backlog.notes: Ninety minutes west of Santiago and the traditional end of the walk. Needs the hire car for one more day than currently booked, which is the only thing stopping it.

backlog.title: An espicha in a Nava cider house
backlog.notes: Standing, unlimited cider poured straight from the barrel, and food brought out in waves. Usually a weekend thing and needs a group; parked until someone finds one that takes two people.
